characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: JEOL 2000FX TEM; thin foils prepared by twin-jet electro-polishing in a mixture of 10% perchloric acid and 90% ethanol with an applied potential of 25 V
characterization_methods.key_findings: TEM BF images used to image nano-sized features such as the cuboid κ particles in the γ matrix and disc-like B2 in α.
characterization_methods.purpose: Characterization of the ordered phases (e.g. cuboid κ particles, disc-like B2)
characterization_methods.technique: Transmission electron microscopy - selected-area diffraction patterns (SADPs) and bright-field (BF) images

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: Carl Zeiss Sigma Field Emission Scanning Electron Microscope operated at 20 kV
characterization_methods.key_findings: Used to observe the micro-scale microstructure (matrix grains, B2 stringer bands, grain-boundary particles).
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Specimens polished and etched in a 5% nital solution

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: High-speed X-ray EDS fitted on the FE-SEM
characterization_methods.key_findings: Used to measure the composition (Ni, Al, Mn content) of particles; e.g. Al content of B2 particles formed in γ was less than those formed in α.
characterization_methods.purpose: Chemical analysis of the phases (e.g. Ni, Mn, Al content in B2 and κ)

characterization_methods.key_findings: For the Ni-free sample at 1050 °C: γ 4 GPa, α 3 GPa, γ+B2 7 GPa, α+B2 8.3 GPa; the technique yields compound hardness values of matrix with particles and cannot measure isolated nano-sized precipitates.
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Constant loading/unloading rate of 500 μN s−1 up to a maximum load of 10000 μN with a hold time of 20 s; each measurement in a particular phase repeated at least 25 times; arrays of 50–70 indentations applied across the region of interest
characterization_methods.purpose: Determination of the nano-hardness of individual phases and combinations of phases (solution-treated γ and α, B2 stringer bands, micrometer-sized and nano-disk B2, and composites γ+κ, γ+κ+microsized B2, γ+microsized B2, α+needle κ, α+nano-disk B2)

analytical_models.equation_role: relates C11 to the longitudinal acoustic velocity
relates C44 to the transverse acoustic velocity
determines C11 and C12 from the volume-conserving orthorhombic distortion energy change
determines C44 from a monoclinic distortion

computational_details.boundary_and_initial_conditions: Brillouin zone integrations with an 18 × 18 × 18 Monkhorst-Pack grid for structure optimization; real-space grid with 50 Ryd energy cut-off for charge density; augmentation charges expanded up to 600 Ryd; 30 × 30 × 30 grid with 60 Ryd cut-off for the electronic density of states and formation energy; Murnaghan equation of state for bulk modulus; density of states calculated by the tetrahedron method with a 30 × 30 × 30 mesh; dynamical matrices from linear response in the harmonic approximation
computational_details.potential_model_or_database: Ultrasoft pseudo-potentials created with a modified Rappe-Rabe-Kaxiras-Joannopoulos (RRKJ) scheme; generalized gradient approximation (GGA) of Perdew-Burke-Ernzerhof (PBE), spin-polarized
computational_details.simulation_method: First-principles DFT calculations (ab-initio) of ordered phases (κ-carbide L1'2, FeAl-B2, Fe3Al-L12) using the Hohenberg-Kohn method
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: Calculated lattice parameter of FeAl-B2 (spin-polarized and non-spin) was slightly less than the experimental value but in good agreement; the calculated lattice constant for Fe3AlC was larger than that of Fe3Al-L12, agreeing with reported experimental observations; the calculated increase in Mn-bearing κ elastic constants confirms the experimentally observed increase in hardness of Mn-enriched κ.

comparative_performance.comparison_metric: nano-hardness of B2-bearing phases/composites (hardness of the B2 phase is higher with Ni due to stronger Ni-Al bonds than Fe-Al bonds)

processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: The experimental alloys were melted in an induction furnace.

processing_steps.method: solution heat treatment followed by water quenching
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Solution heat-treated for 35 min at 1250 °C in a protective argon atmosphere and then water quenched. This is the parent process of the 1050 °C anneal.
The materials were then cut into 3-mm (length), 3-mm (width) and 1-mm (thickness) samples.

Annealing treatments were conducted at 500, 700, 900 and 1050 °C; the 1050 °C state is the highest annealing temperature, selected to study the change in nanomechanical properties arising from an increase in the Ni and Al content of the nanosized disk-like B2 particles. Holding time not explicitly reported.

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Nano-indentation tests carried out at a constant loading/unloading rate of 500 μN s−1 up to a maximum load of 10000 μN with a hold time of 20 s; each measurement repeated at least 25 times; arrays of 50–70 indentations. The technique yields compound hardness of matrix with particles.

hardness.region: α + B2 composite / nanosized disk-like B2 in α

structures.overall_structure: Duplex γ + α microstructure; the Ni-free alloy at 1050 °C consists of a γ + α matrix always containing coarse B2 particles (2–4 μm) and disc-like B2 (≈200 nm).

unmapped_findings: Tables 1 and 2 label the Ni-free alloy as Fe-15Mn-10Al-0.5C (0.5 C) whereas the abstract, introduction, methods and conclusions use Fe-15Mn-10Al-0.8C; the sample_label for this sample is Fe-15Mn-10Al-0.8C per the alloy snapshot, with 'Fe-15Mn-10Al-0.5C, 1050 °C' retained as an alias.

Elemental composition of the B2 particles in the Ni-free sample at 1050 °C from figure_005: nanosized disc-like B2 in α contained ~24.7 wt.% Al (Al content increasing from ~22.9 wt.% at 900 °C), while coarse B2 particles in γ contained ~19.1 wt.% Al (up from ~18.3 wt.% at 900 °C); Al is an α stabiliser so B2 in γ has lower Al than B2 in α.

The Ni-free alloy is reported to be γ + α at all four annealing temperatures (500, 700, 900 and 1050 °C), and the κ-carbide morphology at 1050 °C is not reported — needle-like κ in α (width 200 ± 33 nm at 500 °C, 500 ± 33 nm at 700 °C) is only listed for the two lower annealing temperatures.

Conclusion (b0059): the addition of Ni increased the peak hardness from 7.2 GPa to 9 GPa in both the austenite and ferrite phases — hence the Ni-free sample (this sample) attains the lower peak hardness (7.2 GPa) among B2-bearing composites, whereas the Ni-containing counterpart reaches 9 GPa.

Microstructure micrographs in Figure 2 ((a)–(f)) show the microstructure of the Ni-containing sample; the text (b0018) notes the Ni-free sample followed a similar trend except at lower annealing temperatures (500 and 700 °C) where α + needle-like κ-carbides were observed instead of B2 stringer bands.
